🔥🇲🇽 <u>SUPREME COURT SINKS ANOTHER ELEKTRA AMPARO</u>

Mexico's Supreme Court unanimously denied Salinas Pliego's Nueva Elektra an amparo against the customs processing fee. Elektra wanted to pay the flat 461.61-peso rate that importers covered by trade agreements pay, instead of 8 pesos per 1,000 pesos of goods' value.

Justice Giovanni Figueroa: the difference is "objective and reasonable," set by Mexico's treaty commitments. It's another lost bid by Mexico's loudest tax dodger to rewrite the rules for himself.
banner: ELEKTRA LOSES AGAIN AT SUPREME COURT

🇲🇽🌎 <u>FEMICIDES DOWN 5% AS 100 WOMEN'S CENTERS OPEN</u>

On 25N, Women's Secretary Laura Itzel Castillo reported that Mexico's daily average of femicides fell just over 5% from January to August 2026. "No figure can satisfy us. Every life counts."

The 100 Centros LIBRES planned for 2026 are already open in all 32 states and have served more than 650,000 women. Sheinbaum announced 500 more for 2027.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>USAID FILES PUT CÓRDOVA'S INE IN THE LOOP</u>

Nearly 300 USAID documents, now published by the US State Department, show Mexico's INE under Lorenzo Córdova inside a US-funded "disinformation" network, Contralínea reports.

A 2019 paper from IFES, a USAID-funded electoral NGO, praises INE as "the first electoral body in the world" with memoranda of understanding with Facebook, Twitter and Google, signed for the 2018 elections. Before leaving office in 2023, Córdova toured Washington and met with IFES, the NED, IRI and NDI.

He's now a member of the opposition party Somos.
banner: USAIDGATE: CÓRDOVA'S INE IN THE FILES

text:
🇲🇽🌎 <u>MEXICO POSTS $1.14B CURRENT ACCOUNT SURPLUS</u>

Banxico: Mexico closed Q3 2026 with a current account surplus of $1,142 million, 0.2% of GDP. That's up from $904 million a year earlier and the second straight quarter in the black.

The engine: $16.2 billion in secondary income, mostly remittances sent home by Mexican workers, which more than covered an $8.3 billion goods-and-services deficit.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>DEA LET 1.4 MILLION FENTANYL PILLS HIT THE STREETS</u>

Washington lectures Mexico on fentanyl every week. Meanwhile an AP investigation, reported by La Jornada, found the DEA let at least 1.4 million fentanyl pills circulate between August 2024 and April 2025 while it "tracked" a network in New Mexico, trying to trace the supply back to Mexico.

Most of those pills were never recovered. Albuquerque has filed a $153 million claim against the agency.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>Yokohama Opens Its Biggest Plant in the World, in Coahuila</u>

Japan's Yokohama Rubber opened its tire plant in Derramadero, Saltillo, and announced a second phase. Across both, it is investing about 10 billion pesos for more than 1,500 direct jobs, making it Yokohama's largest plant anywhere, El Economista reports. CEO Masataka Yamaishi credited Saltillo's continuous rail and highway links to the US and its skilled workforce. Coahuila says 222 companies from 19 countries arrived in three years, bringing about 190 billion pesos and 86,000 jobs.
banner: YOKOHAMA: BIGGEST PLANT ON EARTH, COAHUILA

text:
🇲🇽☕ <u>Sheinbaum to Nestlé: Pay Chiapas Coffee Growers a Fair Price</u>

Coffee growers protesting in Tapachula say intermediaries pay them 43 pesos per kilo, and they're asking Nestlé for 50 to 60. They say some 165,000 families depend on the crop. Sheinbaum sided with them: she ordered the Agriculture ministry to join the negotiations, asked Nestlé to buy directly with no middlemen, and asked why the price of finished products like Nescafé never falls in the same proportion. In October, Nestlé pledged to double its Mexico investment to US$2 billion by 2030, with coffee at the center.

🇲🇽⚖️ <u>Mexico City Bets 400 Million Pesos on Prisons That Rehabilitate</u>

Mexico City is launching a Humanist Penitentiary Model and the "Alas de Colibrí" program (Autonomy, Freedom, Accompaniment and Second Chances), with 400 million pesos in 2027 to rebuild its prisons. Schooling through high school, free university courses with public universities, job training with companies, mental health care, and support after release. Clara Brugada: "A society is not more just for having more prisons, nor safer simply for having more people locked up."

🇲🇽🏥 <u>IMSS-Bienestar: 117,000 Health Workers Get Formal Posts on January 1</u>

More than 117,000 health workers will hold a formal position at IMSS-Bienestar from January 1, 2027, with payroll ready December 15, director Alejandro Svarch reported from Toluca, where he opened the agency's first comprehensive kidney-care center. 1,973 new health professionals were hired in the last two weeks alone. "Todo en tu Clínica" has grown from 3,000 to 5,588 health centers in 21 states, with internet, electronic records, digital pharmacy control and free lab tests.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>Sheinbaum: Cartels Are Not Terrorists, and No Treaty Outranks Our Constitution</u>

Fourteen TIAR members voted at the OAS to convene the Cold War-era treaty against "transnational organized crime." Mexico didn't vote: it left the TIAR in 2002. Sheinbaum backed Ambassador Alejandro Encinas and said her government does not share Washington's push to equate organized crime with terrorism, a label that can be used to justify foreign intervention. Asked whether the treaty could be turned against Mexico: "It shouldn't, because it is not above our Constitution."
